title: TRACER: Trajectory-Aware Tool Retrieval for LLM Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.21267v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Modern agents select tools from registries, but exposing entire registries incurs high token costs and can impair selection as they grow. We present TRACER, a retrieval front-end that indexes observed tool-call sequences in a trie and ranks continuations using a learned blend of empirical and contextual priors. On a mixed retail-and-telecom $\tau^2$ environment, TRACER improves GPT-5.4's tool-selection accuracy by 4.7 points while reducing input tokens per step by 80%, exposing just 5 of 128 tools. In autonomous full-turn execution, it matches GPT-5.4's full-registry task success with 61% fewer input tokens per step. Across six environments and four models, TRACER improves tool-selection accuracy over full-registry selection in 21 of 24 model-environment pairs, with average gains of 6 to 10 points; the three exceptions trail by at most 2.2. We analyze failures in both regimes to identify directions for future work.

translated_title: TRACER：面向大语言模型智能体的轨迹感知工具检索
translated_abstract: 现代智能体需要从工具注册表中选择工具，但暴露整个注册表会带来高昂的token成本，且随着注册表规模的增长可能损害选择质量。我们提出了TRACER，这是一个检索前端，它在字典树（trie）中索引观察到的工具调用序列，并使用经验先验与上下文先验的学习混合方式对后续候选工具进行排序。在一个零售与电信混合的τ²环境中，TRACER将GPT-5.4的工具选择准确率提高了4.7个百分点，同时将每步输入token减少了80%，仅暴露128个工具中的5个。在自主的完整回合执行中，它以每步减少61%的输入token实现了与使用全注册表的GPT-5.4相当的任务成功率。在六个环境和四个模型的测试中，TRACER在24个模型-环境对中的21个上将工具选择准确率提升至超过全注册表选择的水平，平均提升6到10个百分点；三个例外情况最多落后2.2个百分点。我们分析了两种模式下的失败案例，以确定未来的研究方向。
tldr: TRACER通过在字典树中索引工具调用序列，并利用经验与上下文先验的学习混合对候选工具排序，在仅暴露极少量工具的情况下，将大语言模型智能体的输入token减少高达80%，同时显著提升工具选择准确率。
en_tdlr: TRACER is a trajectory-aware tool retrieval front-end that indexes tool-call sequences in a trie and ranks continuations using a learned blend of empirical and contextual priors, cutting input tokens by up to 80% while improving tool-selection accuracy for LLM agents.
